Migrate every module in src/services/ (repo root: <run-dir> from callback-style database access to the repository pattern.

Enumerate all modules in src/services/ yourself, then delegate one module per module-migrator worker (run them in parallel where independent). Each worker should migrate its one module to use the matching repository class and run that module's tests.

When done, report back per module: file path, whether migration succeeded, test result (pass/fail with failing test names and error messages if any), and any modules skipped or that lacked a matching repository class (with the reason). Don't summarize away failures — include them verbatim enough that I can relay them.

Paths below are relative to `<run-dir>

| Module | Status | Tests | Blockers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src/services/user-service.js` | complete | 2 passing, 0 failing | See below |
| `src/services/order-service.js` | complete | 2 passing, 0 failing | none |
| `src/services/payment-service.js` | complete | 2 passing, 0 failing | none |
| `src/services/auth-service.js` | complete | 2 passing, 0 failing | none |

The `user-service.js` worker flagged one problem outside its module. `src/api/routes.js` imports `listActiveUsers` and `findUser` and may still call them with callbacks. The worker left that file alone, and I haven't checked it either. If `routes.js` does use callbacks, it will break against the migrated service, and the `user-service.js` tests wouldn't catch that.
